name: Social market economy
summary: The social market economy is the German postwar order of Erhard and Müller-Armack: a competitive market with free prices, independent control of monopolies and a strong state guarding the rules, joined to social security and stable money. It rejects both central planning and laissez-faire. Price stability, free trade and collective wage bargaining are central; the state shapes the framework but does not direct production.
scope: The model as set out by Ludwig Erhard, Alfred Müller-Armack and the CDU Düsseldorf Guidelines of 1949, 1948-1962. It excludes later EU usage of the phrase, and answers only what these texts state. Erhard and Müller-Armack differ on the scope of social compensation and on European institutions.
